An input $c$ with $f(c) = 0$; a real zero is an $x$-intercept of the graph.
A function is increasing on an interval if its graph rises left to right there: $x_1 < x_2$ implies $f(x_1) < f(x_2)$.
A function is decreasing on an interval if its graph falls left to right there: $x_1 < x_2$ implies $f(x_1) > f(x_2)$.
A function is constant on an interval if it has the same output for every input there.
A value $f(c)$ at least as large as all nearby values of $f$: the top of a hill.
A value $f(c)$ no larger than all nearby values of $f$: the bottom of a valley.
Local maxima and local minima together.
The largest value a function takes on its whole domain, if there is one.
The smallest value a function takes on its whole domain, if there is one.
The change in output over the change in input, $\dfrac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$; the slope of the secant line.
A line through two points of a graph; its slope is the average rate of change between them.
$\dfrac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}$, the average rate of change from $x$ to $x + h$.
The basic functions ($x$, $x^2$, $x^3$, $\sqrt x$, $\sqrt[3]{x}$, $|x|$, $\frac1x$, $b^x$, $\log_b x$, …) that other functions transform.
A function with $f(-x) = f(x)$ for all $x$ in its domain; its graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.
A function with $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for all $x$ in its domain; its graph has origin symmetry.
A graph has origin symmetry if rotating it 180° about the origin leaves it unchanged: $(a, b)$ on it means $(-a, -b)$ is too.
A shift, reflection, stretch or compression that moves or reshapes a graph.
A transformation that slides a graph without changing its shape.
A transformation that flips a graph over a line: $-f(x)$ reflects over the $x$-axis, $f(-x)$ over the $y$-axis.
$y = f(x) + k$ moves the graph up $k$ units (down if $k < 0$).
$y = af(x)$ with $|a| > 1$ multiplies every output by $a$, pulling the graph away from the $x$-axis.
$y = af(x)$ with $0 < |a| < 1$ squeezes the graph toward the $x$-axis.
$y = f(x - h)$ moves the graph right $h$ units (left if $h < 0$).
$y = f(bx)$ with $|b| > 1$ squeezes the graph toward the $y$-axis by a factor $\frac{1}{|b|}$ (and also reflects it over the $y$-axis if $b < 0$).
$y = f(bx)$ with $0 < |b| < 1$ stretches the graph away from the $y$-axis by a factor $\frac{1}{|b|}$ (and also reflects it over the $y$-axis if $b < 0$).
$(f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))$: apply $g$ first, then $f$.
A function in which different inputs always give different outputs; it passes the horizontal line test.
A function is one-to-one exactly when no horizontal line meets its graph more than once.
The function $f^{-1}$ that undoes $f$: $f^{-1}(y) = x$ exactly when $f(x) = y$. Its graph is the reflection of $f$ across $y = x$.
A function $a_nx^n + \dots + a_1x + a_0$ with whole-number exponents; smooth and unbroken, with domain all reals.
The highest power of the variable in a polynomial with a nonzero coefficient.
The term of a polynomial with the highest power, $a_nx^n$; it controls end behavior.
The coefficient $a_n$ of the leading term.
What $f(x)$ does as $x \to \infty$ and $x \to -\infty$.
The number of times a factor $(x - c)$ appears. Odd multiplicity: the graph crosses at $c$; even: it touches and turns.
A point where a graph changes from rising to falling or vice versa; degree $n$ allows at most $n - 1$.
If $f$ is continuous on $[a, b]$ and $f(a)$, $f(b)$ have opposite signs, then $f$ has a zero between $a$ and $b$ (more generally, it takes every value between $f(a)$ and $f(b)$).
For polynomials, $f(x) = d(x)q(x) + r(x)$ with $r = 0$ or $\deg r < \deg d$.
The result $q(x)$ of dividing one polynomial by another.
What is left over in a division, of lower degree than the divisor.
A shortcut for dividing a polynomial by $x - c$ using only coefficients.
When $f(x)$ is divided by $x - c$, the remainder is $f(c)$.
$x - c$ is a factor of $f(x)$ exactly when $f(c) = 0$.
The quotient left after dividing out a known zero; its degree is one less.
If $\frac pq$ (lowest terms) is a zero of an integer-coefficient polynomial, then $p$ divides the constant term and $q$ divides the leading coefficient.
The number of positive real zeros equals the number of sign changes in the coefficients, or is less than it by an even number.
Every polynomial of degree $n \ge 1$ has at least one complex zero; hence exactly $n$ zeros counting multiplicity.
A degree-$n$ polynomial factors as $a_n(x - c_1)\cdots(x - c_n)$ with complex $c_k$.
The conjugate of $a + bi$ is $a - bi$.
If a polynomial has real coefficients and $a + bi$ is a zero, then $a - bi$ is also a zero.
A quotient of two polynomials, $\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$.
A single missing point on a graph, from a factor that cancels in a rational function (a removable discontinuity).
A vertical line $x = a$ near which $|f(x)| \to \infty$; for a reduced rational function, a zero of the denominator.
A horizontal line $y = L$ that the graph approaches as $x \to \infty$ or $x \to -\infty$.
A non-horizontal line approached at the ends of a graph; for a rational function with numerator degree one more than the denominator, the quotient from division.
In an inequality, the zeros of the numerator and denominator, where the sign can change.
A number line marked with critical values and the sign of an expression on each interval.
$f(x) = b^x$ with $b > 0$, $b \ne 1$: the variable is in the exponent.
Growth by a constant factor greater than 1 per unit of time.
Shrinking by a constant factor between 0 and 1 per unit of time.
The amount of money initially invested or borrowed.
Interest added to the balance periodically, so later interest is earned on earlier interest: $A = P\left(1 + \frac rn\right)^{nt}$.
The constant $e \approx 2.71828$, the limit of $\left(1 + \frac1n\right)^n$.
Interest compounded at every instant: $A = Pe^{rt}$.
The function $e^x$.
$\log_b x$ is the exponent you put on $b$ to get $x$: $\log_b x = y \iff b^y = x$.
The base-10 logarithm, written $\log x$.
The base-$e$ logarithm, written $\ln x$.
$\log_b x = \dfrac{\ln x}{\ln b} = \dfrac{\log x}{\log b}$.
A value produced by solving that does not satisfy the original equation (for example, one that makes a log argument nonpositive).
The constant $k$ in $Q = Q_0e^{kt}$; positive for growth, negative for decay.
The time for an exponentially growing quantity to double: $\frac{\ln 2}{k}$.
The time for a decaying quantity to fall to half its amount.
An object's temperature approaches the surrounding temperature exponentially: $T = T_s + (T_0 - T_s)e^{-kt}$.
$P = \dfrac{C}{1 + Ae^{-kt}}$: growth that starts nearly exponential and levels off at the carrying capacity $C$.
The maximum value $C$ that a logistic model approaches.
An angle measure: arc length divided by radius. A full turn is $2\pi$ radians, so $180^\circ = \pi$.
The length of an arc of a circle: $s = r\theta$ with $\theta$ in radians.
The circle $x^2 + y^2 = 1$; the point at angle $\theta$ is $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$.
An angle with vertex at the origin and initial side on the positive $x$-axis; a vector drawn starting at the origin.
$\sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta}$, $\csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta}$, $\cot\theta = \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$.
The acute angle between an angle's terminal side and the $x$-axis.
A function is periodic if its values repeat at regular intervals: $f(x + p) = f(x)$.
The length of the smallest interval after which a periodic function repeats; $\frac{2\pi}{|B|}$ for $\sin(Bx)$.
A transformed sine or cosine curve, $y = A\sin(B(x - C)) + D$.
Half the distance between the maximum and minimum of a sinusoid: $|A|$.
The horizontal shift $C$ of a sinusoid $y = A\sin(B(x - C)) + D$.
The horizontal line $y = D$ halfway between a sinusoid's maximum and minimum.
An equation that is true for every input for which both sides are defined.
An equation like $ax + by + cz = d$ in which each variable appears to the first power only.
Several linear equations to be satisfied at the same time.
A system with no solution.
A consistent system with infinitely many solutions.
A rectangular array of numbers arranged in rows and columns.
The matrix of a system's coefficients with an extra column of constants.
Swapping two rows, multiplying a row by a nonzero constant, or adding a multiple of one row to another.
Using row operations to reach row-echelon form, then back-substituting.
A staircase matrix form: zero rows at the bottom, each pivot to the right of the one above, zeros below each pivot.
The first nonzero entry in a row of a row-echelon matrix.
Solving the last equation first and substituting upward.
Row-echelon form in which every pivot is 1 and is the only nonzero entry in its column.
Row reduction all the way to reduced row-echelon form.
A variable without a pivot, which can take any value in a dependent system.
The size of a matrix, rows × columns.
One number in a matrix; $a_{ij}$ is in row $i$, column $j$.
A matrix with the same number of rows and columns.
A single real number, as opposed to a vector or matrix.
A matrix whose entries are all 0, written $O$.
Multiply matching components and add: $\vec u \cdot \vec v = u_1v_1 + u_2v_2 + \cdots$; a number.
The square matrix $I$ with 1s on the main diagonal and 0s elsewhere; $AI = IA = A$.
A square matrix $A$ is invertible if some $A^{-1}$ satisfies $AA^{-1} = A^{-1}A = I$.
The matrix $A^{-1}$ with $AA^{-1} = A^{-1}A = I$.
A square matrix with no inverse; its determinant is 0.
A number computed from a square matrix; for $2 \times 2$, $ad - bc$. It is nonzero exactly when the matrix is invertible.
The determinant left after deleting an entry's row and column.
A minor with the checkerboard sign: $C_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}$.
Computing a determinant by multiplying each entry of one row or column by its cofactor and adding.
For $AX = B$ with $D = \det A \ne 0$: $x_i = \frac{D_i}{D}$, where $D_i$ replaces column $i$ with the constants.
Rewriting a rational expression as a sum of simpler fractions with linear or irreducible quadratic denominators.
A rational expression whose numerator degree is at least the denominator degree; divide before decomposing.
A rational expression whose numerator has lower degree than its denominator.
Curves made by slicing a double cone with a plane: circles, ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas.
The set of points equidistant from a focus and a directrix.
A fixed point used to define a conic: one for a parabola, two for an ellipse or hyperbola.
The fixed line in the focus-directrix definition of a conic.
A turning point of a parabola, or an endpoint of the major (ellipse) or transverse (hyperbola) axis.
The line through a parabola's focus and vertex, perpendicular to the directrix.
The length $|4p|$ of the chord through a parabola's focus parallel to the directrix.
The set of points whose distances to two foci add to a constant $2a$.
The midpoint of the foci of an ellipse or hyperbola (or the center of a circle).
The longest chord of an ellipse, through both foci; its length is $2a$.
The chord of an ellipse through the center perpendicular to the major axis; length $2b$.
The endpoints of an ellipse's minor axis.
The number $e = \frac ca$ (or the focus-directrix ratio) that measures how far a conic is from circular: $e = 0$ circle, $e < 1$ ellipse, $e = 1$ parabola, $e > 1$ hyperbola.
The set of points at a fixed distance $r$ from a center: $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$.
The set of points whose distances to two foci differ by a constant $2a$ in absolute value.
The segment joining a hyperbola's two vertices.
The rectangle of sides $2a$ and $2b$ centered at a hyperbola's center; its diagonals extend to the asymptotes.
Point, line or line-pair graphs (or no graph) given by a second-degree equation.
For a quadratic, $b^2 - 4ac$ (its sign counts real roots). For a conic $Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + \dots = 0$, $B^2 - 4AC$: negative ellipse, zero parabola, positive hyperbola.
Equations $x = f(t)$, $y = g(t)$ giving both coordinates in terms of a parameter.
The third variable (often $t$) in parametric equations; it orders the points of the curve.
The direction a parametric curve is traced as the parameter increases.
Coordinates $(r, \theta)$: distance $r$ from the pole in direction $\theta$.
The origin of a polar coordinate system.
The ray from the pole (the positive $x$-axis) from which polar angles are measured.
A polar curve $r = a + b\cos\theta$ or $a + b\sin\theta$.
A heart-shaped limaçon, with $|a| = |b|$, passing through the pole.
A polar curve $r = a\cos n\theta$ or $a\sin n\theta$: $n$ petals if $n$ is odd, $2n$ if $n$ is even.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, drawn as an arrow or written $\langle a, b \rangle$.
A segment with an initial point and a terminal point, representing a vector.
The length of a vector: $\lVert\langle a, b\rangle\rVert = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$.
Writing a vector as $\langle a, b \rangle$ (or $\langle a, b, c \rangle$), the coordinates of its tip in standard position.
The sum of two or more vectors, such as a net force or a ground velocity.
A vector of magnitude 1; $\frac{\vec v}{\lVert\vec v\rVert}$ points the same way as $\vec v$.
The angle a vector makes counterclockwise from the positive $x$-axis.
Perpendicular; two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is 0.
The part of $\vec u$ along $\vec v$: $\text{proj}_{\vec v}\vec u = \frac{\vec u \cdot \vec v}{\lVert\vec v\rVert^2}\vec v$.
The signed length $\frac{\vec u \cdot \vec v}{\lVert\vec v\rVert}$ of the projection of $\vec u$ on $\vec v$.
Force times displacement in the direction of motion: $W = \vec F \cdot \vec d$.
For 3D vectors, $\vec u \times \vec v$, a vector orthogonal to both, with magnitude equal to the area of their parallelogram.
A function on the positive integers, written $a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots$
One entry $a_n$ of a sequence (or one addend of a sum).
A formula that gives $a_n$ directly from $n$.
A starting term plus a rule giving each term from earlier ones.
$1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, \dots$, where each term is the sum of the two before it.
$n! = n(n - 1)\cdots 2 \cdot 1$, with $0! = 1$.
The sum of the terms of a sequence.
$\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_k$, shorthand for $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n$.
The variable (such as $k$) that runs through the integer values in sigma notation.
A sequence with a constant difference $d$: $a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d$.
The constant $d = a_{n+1} - a_n$ of an arithmetic sequence.
A sequence with a constant ratio $r$: $a_n = a_1r^{n-1}$.
The constant $r = \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}$ of a geometric sequence.
An infinite series converges if its partial sums approach a finite number.
An infinite series diverges if its partial sums do not approach a finite number.
Proving $P(n)$ for all $n \ge n_0$ by proving a base case and that $P(k)$ implies $P(k + 1)$.
The first statement, such as $P(1)$, checked directly in an induction proof.
The part of an induction proof showing that $P(k)$ implies $P(k + 1)$.
The assumption that $P(k)$ is true, used to prove $P(k + 1)$.
The triangle of binomial coefficients, where each entry is the sum of the two above it.
$\binom nk = \frac{n!}{k!(n - k)!}$, the coefficient of $a^{n-k}b^k$ in $(a + b)^n$ and the number of ways to choose $k$ of $n$ items.
In $(a + b)^n$, the term $\binom nk a^{n-k}b^k$ (the $(k + 1)$st term).
$(a + b)^n = \sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom nk a^{n-k}b^k$.
If a task has stages with $m_1, m_2, \dots$ choices, the total number of ways is $m_1 m_2\cdots$.
An ordered arrangement; $_nP_r = \frac{n!}{(n - r)!}$.
An unordered selection; $_nC_r = \frac{n!}{r!(n - r)!}$.
The set of all possible outcomes of an experiment.
A set of outcomes from the sample space.
The event "not $E$": all outcomes not in $E$; $P(\text{not } E) = 1 - P(E)$.
Events that cannot happen at the same time: $P(A \text{ and } B) = 0$.
Events where one happening does not change the probability of the other: $P(A \text{ and } B) = P(A)P(B)$.
$\lim_{x\to a}f(x) = L$ means $f(x)$ gets as close to $L$ as we like when $x$ is close enough to (but not equal to) $a$.
$\lim_{x\to a^-}f(x)$, the limit using only $x < a$.
$\lim_{x\to a^+}f(x)$, the limit using only $x > a$.
$f$ is continuous at $a$ if $\lim_{x\to a}f(x) = f(a)$: the graph has no break there.
A point where a function is not continuous: a hole, a jump, or a vertical asymptote.
A hole: the limit exists but $f(a)$ is undefined or different; redefining one point fixes it.
Finding a limit by plugging in $x = a$; valid when $f$ is continuous at $a$.
An expression like $\frac00$ from substitution that does not determine the limit; more algebra is needed.
The line through a point on a curve with the curve's slope there; the limit of secant lines.
$f'(a) = \lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(a + h) - f(a)}{h}$, the slope of the tangent line at $a$.
The rate of change at a single instant, given by the derivative.
$f'(x)$, giving the slope of $f$ at each $x$.
Memory aid for right-triangle trig: Sine = Opposite/Hypotenuse, Cosine = Adjacent/Hypotenuse, Tangent = Opposite/Adjacent.
Memory aid for which trig functions are positive in Quadrants I–IV: All, Sine, Tangent, Cosine.
The line through $(x_1, y_1)$ with slope $m$: $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$.
A connected set of real numbers, such as $[a, b]$ or $(a, \infty)$.
A quadratic with no real zeros (negative discriminant), so it has no real linear factors.
A series of equal regular payments or deposits; its value is a geometric series.
A sum in which consecutive terms cancel, leaving only a few terms, as in $\sum\left(\frac1k - \frac1{k+1}\right)$.
Sine and cosine (likewise tangent and cotangent) are cofunctions: $\cos x = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)$.
$\sin^{-1}$, $\cos^{-1}$, $\tan^{-1}$: inverses of trig functions on restricted domains, returning angles.
A line that a graph approaches more and more closely.

references.title: Functions, graphs and polynomials
references.body:
## Domain and notation

| Feature in the formula | Domain restriction |
|---|---|
| $\dfrac{p(x)}{q(x)}$ | $q(x) \ne 0$ |
| $\sqrt{u}$, $\sqrt[4]{u}$ (even roots) | $u \ge 0$ |
| $\log_b u$, $\ln u$ | $u > 0$ |
| $\sqrt[3]{u}$ (odd roots), polynomials | none |

| Interval | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $[a, b]$ | $a \le x \le b$ |
| $(a, b)$ | $a < x < b$ |
| $[a, \infty)$ | $x \ge a$ |
| $A \cup B$ | in $A$ or in $B$ |

## Rates of change

| Quantity | Formula |
|---|---|
| Average rate of change on $[a, b]$ | $\dfrac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$ (slope of secant) |
| Difference quotient | $\dfrac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}$ |
| Vertex of $ax^2 + bx + c$ | $x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$ |

## Symmetry

| Type | Test | Graph |
|---|---|---|
| Even | $f(-x) = f(x)$ | symmetric about the $y$-axis |
| Odd | $f(-x) = -f(x)$ | symmetric about the origin |

## Transformations of $y = f(x)$

| Equation | Effect |
|---|---|
| $y = f(x) + k$ | up $k$ (down if $k < 0$) |
| $y = f(x - h)$ | right $h$ (left if $h < 0$) |
| $y = -f(x)$ | reflect over the $x$-axis |
| $y = f(-x)$ | reflect over the $y$-axis |
| $y = a f(x)$ | vertical stretch by $\lvert a \rvert$ ($\lvert a \rvert > 1$) or compression ($\lvert a \rvert < 1$) |
| $y = f(bx)$ | horizontal compression by factor $1/\lvert b \rvert$ ($\lvert b \rvert > 1$) or stretch ($\lvert b \rvert < 1$); reflect over the $y$-axis too if $b < 0$ |
| $y = a f(b(x - h)) + k$ | point $(p, q) \mapsto \left(\tfrac{p}{b} + h,\; aq + k\right)$ |

## Composition and inverses

- $(f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))$; domain: $x$ in domain of $g$ with $g(x)$ in domain of $f$.
- $f^{-1}$ exists when $f$ is one-to-one (horizontal line test).
- $f(f^{-1}(x)) = x$ and $f^{-1}(f(x)) = x$; graphs mirror across $y = x$.
- To find $f^{-1}$: write $y = f(x)$, swap $x$ and $y$, solve for $y$.

## Polynomials

| Fact | Statement |
|---|---|
| End behavior | follows the leading term $a_n x^n$ |
| Turning points | at most $n - 1$ |
| Multiplicity | odd: graph crosses; even: graph touches and turns |
| Remainder theorem | $f(x) \div (x - c)$ leaves remainder $f(c)$ |
| Factor theorem | $(x - c)$ is a factor $\iff f(c) = 0$ |
| Rational zeros | $\pm\dfrac{\text{factor of } a_0}{\text{factor of } a_n}$ |
| Fundamental theorem | degree $n$ has exactly $n$ complex zeros (with multiplicity) |
| Conjugates | real coefficients: $a + bi$ zero $\Rightarrow$ $a - bi$ zero |

## Rational functions $R(x) = \dfrac{p(x)}{q(x)}$ (reduced)

| Degrees | Horizontal asymptote |
|---|---|
| $\deg p < \deg q$ | $y = 0$ |
| $\deg p = \deg q$ | $y = \dfrac{\text{leading coeff of } p}{\text{leading coeff of } q}$ |
| $\deg p = \deg q + 1$ | none; slant asymptote = quotient of $p \div q$ |

- Common factor cancels: hole. Remaining zero of the denominator: vertical asymptote.
- Inequalities: move everything to one side, find zeros and undefined points, test each interval (sign chart).

references.title: Exponentials, logarithms and trig review
references.body:
## Exponential functions

| Fact | Formula |
|---|---|
| Exponential function | $f(x) = b^x$, $b > 0$, $b \ne 1$; through $(0, 1)$; asymptote $y = 0$ |
| Growth / decay | $b > 1$ grows; $0 < b < 1$ decays |
| Compound interest | $A = P\left(1 + \dfrac{r}{n}\right)^{nt}$ |
| Continuous compounding | $A = Pe^{rt}$ |
| Natural base | $e = \lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left(1 + \tfrac1n\right)^n \approx 2.71828$ |

## Logarithms

| Rule | Formula |
|---|---|
| Definition | $\log_b x = y \iff b^y = x$ ($x > 0$) |
| Special values | $\log_b 1 = 0$, $\log_b b = 1$ |
| Inverse properties | $\log_b b^x = x$, $b^{\log_b x} = x$ |
| Product | $\log_b(MN) = \log_b M + \log_b N$ |
| Quotient | $\log_b\dfrac MN = \log_b M - \log_b N$ |
| Power | $\log_b M^p = p\log_b M$ |
| Change of base | $\log_b x = \dfrac{\ln x}{\ln b}$ |
| Common / natural | $\log x = \log_{10} x$, $\ln x = \log_e x$ |

## Solving equations

| Type | Method |
|---|---|
| $b^{u} = b^{v}$ | $u = v$ |
| $a \cdot b^{x} = c$ | $x = \dfrac{\ln(c/a)}{\ln b}$ |
| $b^{2x}$ and $b^x$ | substitute $u = b^x$ |
| $\log_b u = k$ | $u = b^k$; check for extraneous solutions |

## Models

| Model | Formula |
|---|---|
| Exponential | $Q = Q_0e^{kt}$ |
| Doubling time | $T = \dfrac{\ln 2}{k}$ |
| Half-life $T$ | $Q = Q_0\left(\tfrac12\right)^{t/T}$, $k = -\dfrac{\ln 2}{T}$ |
| Newton's cooling | $T = T_s + (T_0 - T_s)e^{-kt}$ |
| Logistic | $P = \dfrac{C}{1 + Ae^{-kt}}$, $A = \dfrac{C}{P_0} - 1$, half capacity at $t = \dfrac{\ln A}{k}$ |

## Trigonometry review

| Angle | $0$ | $\frac{\pi}{6}$ | $\frac{\pi}{4}$ | $\frac{\pi}{3}$ | $\frac{\pi}{2}$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $\sin$ | $0$ | $\frac12$ | $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$ | $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ | $1$ |
| $\cos$ | $1$ | $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ | $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$ | $\frac12$ | $0$ |
| $\tan$ | $0$ | $\frac{\sqrt3}{3}$ | $1$ | $\sqrt3$ | undefined |

| Fact | Formula |
|---|---|
| Degrees to radians | multiply by $\dfrac{\pi}{180}$ |
| Unit circle | $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$; $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ |
| Sinusoid | $y = A\sin(B(x - C)) + D$: amplitude $\lvert A \rvert$, period $\dfrac{2\pi}{\lvert B \rvert}$, phase shift $C$, midline $y = D$ |
| Pythagorean | $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$, $1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta$ |
| Sum | $\sin(a \pm b) = \sin a\cos b \pm \cos a \sin b$; $\cos(a \pm b) = \cos a \cos b \mp \sin a \sin b$ |
| Double angle | $\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$; $\cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta$ |
| Even / odd | $\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta$; $\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta$ |

references.title: Matrices, sequences, counting and limits
references.body:
## Systems and matrices

| Idea | Rule |
|---|---|
| Row operations | swap rows; multiply a row by $k \ne 0$; add a multiple of one row to another |
| No solution | a row $[0 \cdots 0 \mid c]$ with $c \ne 0$ |
| Infinitely many | fewer pivots than variables (free variables), no contradiction |
| Product size | $(m \times n)(n \times p) = m \times p$ |
| Product entry | $(AB)_{ij}$ = row $i$ of $A$ · column $j$ of $B$ |
| Identity | $AI = IA = A$ |
| $2 \times 2$ determinant | $\begin{vmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{vmatrix} = ad - bc$ |
| $2 \times 2$ inverse | $\dfrac{1}{ad - bc}\begin{bmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{bmatrix}$ |
| General inverse | row-reduce $[A \mid I] \to [I \mid A^{-1}]$ |
| Solve $AX = B$ | $X = A^{-1}B$ |
| Cramer's rule | $x_i = \dfrac{D_i}{D}$ ($D_i$: column $i$ replaced by constants) |
| Triangle area | $\tfrac12\left\lvert\det\begin{bmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\right\rvert$ |

## Partial fractions

| Factor | Terms |
|---|---|
| $(x - a)$ | $\dfrac{A}{x - a}$ |
| $(x - a)^k$ | $\dfrac{A_1}{x - a} + \dots + \dfrac{A_k}{(x - a)^k}$ |
| irreducible $x^2 + bx + c$ | $\dfrac{Bx + C}{x^2 + bx + c}$ |

## Sequences and series

| Type | $n$th term | Sum |
|---|---|---|
| Arithmetic | $a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d$ | $S_n = \dfrac{n(a_1 + a_n)}{2}$ |
| Geometric | $a_n = a_1 r^{n - 1}$ | $S_n = a_1\dfrac{1 - r^n}{1 - r}$ |
| Infinite geometric | ($\lvert r \rvert < 1$) | $S = \dfrac{a_1}{1 - r}$ |

| Sum | Formula |
|---|---|
| $\sum_{k=1}^n k$ | $\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$ |
| $\sum_{k=1}^n k^2$ | $\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}$ |
| $\sum_{k=1}^n k^3$ | $\left(\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)^2$ |

## Counting, binomial theorem, probability

| Idea | Formula |
|---|---|
| Permutations | $_nP_r = \dfrac{n!}{(n - r)!}$ (order matters) |
| Combinations | $_nC_r = \dbinom{n}{r} = \dfrac{n!}{r!(n - r)!}$ (order doesn't) |
| Binomial theorem | $(a + b)^n = \sum_{k=0}^{n}\dbinom{n}{k}a^{n-k}b^k$ |
| Complement | $P(\text{not } A) = 1 - P(A)$ |
| Addition rule | $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$ |
| Independent events | $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$ |

## Limits and the derivative

| Idea | Statement |
|---|---|
| Limit exists | $\lim_{x\to a^-}f(x) = \lim_{x\to a^+}f(x)$ |
| Continuity at $a$ | $\lim_{x\to a}f(x) = f(a)$ |
| $\tfrac00$ forms | factor and cancel, or rationalize |
| Rational at $\infty$ | compare degrees (same as horizontal asymptotes) |
| Derivative | $f'(a) = \lim\limits_{h\to 0}\dfrac{f(a + h) - f(a)}{h}$ |
| Tangent line | $y = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)$ |

references.title: Conics, parametric, polar and vectors
references.body:
## Conic sections (center or vertex at $(h, k)$)

| Conic | Standard form | Key facts |
|---|---|---|
| Parabola (up/down) | $(x - h)^2 = 4p(y - k)$ | focus $(h, k + p)$, directrix $y = k - p$ |
| Parabola (right/left) | $(y - k)^2 = 4p(x - h)$ | focus $(h + p, k)$, directrix $x = h - p$ |
| Circle | $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$ | $e = 0$ |
| Ellipse (horizontal) | $\dfrac{(x - h)^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{(y - k)^2}{b^2} = 1$, $a > b$ | $c^2 = a^2 - b^2$; vertices $(h \pm a, k)$; foci $(h \pm c, k)$ |
| Ellipse (vertical) | $\dfrac{(x - h)^2}{b^2} + \dfrac{(y - k)^2}{a^2} = 1$ | vertices $(h, k \pm a)$; foci $(h, k \pm c)$ |
| Hyperbola (left/right) | $\dfrac{(x - h)^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{(y - k)^2}{b^2} = 1$ | $c^2 = a^2 + b^2$; asymptotes $y - k = \pm\frac ba(x - h)$ |
| Hyperbola (up/down) | $\dfrac{(y - k)^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{(x - h)^2}{b^2} = 1$ | asymptotes $y - k = \pm\frac ab(x - h)$ |

| Eccentricity $e = \frac ca$ | Conic |
|---|---|
| $e = 0$ | circle |
| $0 < e < 1$ | ellipse |
| $e = 1$ | parabola |
| $e > 1$ | hyperbola |

General form $Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0$: $B^2 - 4AC < 0$ ellipse, $= 0$ parabola, $> 0$ hyperbola. Rotation angle: $\cot 2\theta = \dfrac{A - C}{B}$.

## Parametric equations

| Curve | Parametrization |
|---|---|
| Segment $(x_1, y_1) \to (x_2, y_2)$ | $x = x_1 + (x_2 - x_1)t$, $y = y_1 + (y_2 - y_1)t$, $0 \le t \le 1$ |
| Circle / ellipse | $x = h + a\cos t$, $y = k + b\sin t$ |
| Projectile (m, s) | $x = v_x t$, $y = h_0 + v_y t - 4.9t^2$ |

## Polar coordinates

| Conversion | Formula |
|---|---|
| Polar to rectangular | $x = r\cos\theta$, $y = r\sin\theta$ |
| Rectangular to polar | $r^2 = x^2 + y^2$, $\tan\theta = \frac yx$ (check quadrant) |
| Same point | $(r, \theta) = (r, \theta + 2\pi) = (-r, \theta + \pi)$ |

| Polar graph | Shape |
|---|---|
| $r = a$ | circle about the pole |
| $r = 2a\cos\theta$ | circle through the pole |
| $r = a + b\cos\theta$ | limaçon (cardioid if $\lvert a\rvert = \lvert b\rvert$) |
| $r = a\cos n\theta$ | rose: $n$ petals ($n$ odd), $2n$ petals ($n$ even) |
| $r = \dfrac{ed}{1 \pm e\cos\theta}$, $\dfrac{ed}{1 \pm e\sin\theta}$ | conic with focus at the pole |

## Vectors

| Idea | Formula |
|---|---|
| Component form | $\vec{PQ} = \langle x_2 - x_1, y_2 - y_1 \rangle$ |
| Magnitude | $\lVert\langle a, b\rangle\rVert = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$; in 3D $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2}$ |
| From magnitude and angle | $\vec v = \langle \lVert\vec v\rVert\cos\theta, \lVert\vec v\rVert\sin\theta \rangle$ |
| Unit vector | $\dfrac{\vec v}{\lVert\vec v\rVert}$ |
| Dot product | $\vec u \cdot \vec v = u_1v_1 + u_2v_2 (+ u_3v_3) = \lVert\vec u\rVert\lVert\vec v\rVert\cos\theta$ |
| Angle | $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\vec u \cdot \vec v}{\lVert\vec u\rVert\lVert\vec v\rVert}$ |
| Orthogonal | $\vec u \cdot \vec v = 0$ |
| Projection | $\text{proj}_{\vec v}\vec u = \dfrac{\vec u \cdot \vec v}{\lVert\vec v\rVert^2}\vec v$ |
| Work | $W = \vec F \cdot \vec d$ |
| Distance in 3D | $\sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2 + (z_2 - z_1)^2}$ |
| Cross product | $\vec u \times \vec v = \langle u_2v_3 - u_3v_2,\ u_3v_1 - u_1v_3,\ u_1v_2 - u_2v_1\rangle$ |

drills.title: Evaluate a function
drills.prompt: Let $f(x) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$. Find $f({t})$.

drills.title: Domain of a square root function
drills.prompt: The domain of $f(x) = \sqrt{{a:coef}x {b:signed}}$ is $x {dir} p$ for some number $p$. Find $p$ as an exact fraction or integer.
drills.solution: The radicand must be nonnegative: ${a:coef}x {b:signed} \ge 0$, so ${a}x \ge {nb}$. Divide by ${a}$ (dividing by a negative number flips the inequality): $x {dir} {ep:texfrac}$. So $p =$ **{ep:frac}**.

drills.title: Excluded values of a rational function
drills.prompt: The domain of $g(x) = \dfrac{x {c:signed}}{x^2 {p:signedcoef}x {q:signed}}$ is all real numbers except two values. Find them (smaller first).
drills.solution: Set the denominator to zero and factor: $x^2 {p:signedcoef}x {q:signed} = (x {nr1:signed})(x {nr2:signed}) = 0$. The excluded values are **{r1}** and **{r2}**. (The numerator's zero does not matter for the domain.)

drills.title: Evaluate a piecewise function

choices.label: less than the break point, so the first formula applies
at or above the break point, so the second formula applies

drills.prompt:
Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} {a:coef}x {b:signed} & \text{if } x < {k} \\ x^2 {c:signed} & \text{if } x \ge {k} \end{cases}$

Find $f({t})$.
drills.solution: The input {t} is {side}. Using that formula with $x = {t}$ gives $f({t}) =$ **{val}**.

drills.title: Solve an absolute value equation
drills.prompt: Solve $|{a}x {b:signed}| = {c}$. Give both solutions, smaller first.
drills.solution: The inside equals ${c}$ or ${nc}$. From ${a}x {b:signed} = {nc}$: $x =$ **{x1}**. From ${a}x {b:signed} = {c}$: $x =$ **{x2}**.

drills.title: Average rate of change of a quadratic
drills.prompt: Find the average rate of change of $f(x) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$ on the interval $[{p}, {q}]$.
drills.solution: $f({q}) = {fq}$ and $f({p}) = {fp}$, so the rate is $\dfrac{ {fq} - ({fp}) }{ {q} - ({p}) } =$ **{rate}**.

drills.title: Simplify a difference quotient
drills.prompt: Simplify the difference quotient $\dfrac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}$ for $f(x) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$. Use $x$ and $h$.
drills.solution: $f(x+h) - f(x) = {a}\big[(x+h)^2 - x^2\big] + ({b})\big[(x+h) - x\big] = {a}(2xh + h^2) + ({b})h$. The constant {c} cancels. Divide by $h$: **${a2}x {a:signedcoef}h {b:signed}$**.

drills.title: Maximum or minimum of a quadratic
drills.prompt: Find where $f(x) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$ reaches its extreme value, and what that value is.
drills.solution: $x = \dfrac{-b}{2a} = \dfrac{ {na} }{ {a2} } =$ **{xv}**. Then $f({xv}) =$ **{yv}**. Since the leading coefficient is {a}, this is a {s}.

drills.title: One-sided limits of a piecewise function
drills.prompt:
Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} {a:coef}x {b:signed} & x < {c} \\ {p:coef}x^2 {q:signed} & x \ge {c} \end{cases}$

Find $\lim_{x\to {c}^-} f(x)$ and $\lim_{x\to {c}^+} f(x)$. Then type 1 if the two-sided limit exists, 0 if not.
drills.solution: From the left use ${a:coef}x {b:signed}$: $({a})({c}) + ({b}) =$ **{L}**. From the right use ${p:coef}x^2 {q:signed}$: $({p})({c})^2 + ({q}) =$ **{R}**. The limit exists only if these agree, so the answer is **{same}**.

drills.title: Estimate a limit numerically
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\dfrac{\sin({k}x)}{x}$ at $x = 0.1, 0.01, 0.001$ (radians) and use the trend to find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sin({k}x)}{x}$.
drills.solution: The values are about {v1:num4}, {v2:num4}, {v3:num4} (and the same from the left, since the function is even), approaching **{k}**. Near 0, $\sin({k}x) \approx {k}x$, so the quotient is close to {k}.

drills.title: Limit by factoring
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to {a}}\frac{x^2 {s:signedcoef}x {pr:signed}}{x {na:signed}}$.
drills.solution: Substitution gives $\frac00$. Factor the numerator: $(x {na:signed})(x {b:signed})$. Cancel $(x {na:signed})$ and substitute: ${a} + ({b}) =$ **{L}**.

drills.title: Limit by rationalizing
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{x + {c2}} - {c}}{x}$ as an exact fraction.
drills.solution: Multiply by the conjugate: $\dfrac{(x + {c2}) - {c2}}{x\left(\sqrt{x + {c2}} + {c}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x + {c2}} + {c}}$. At $x = 0$: $\dfrac{1}{ {c} + {c} } = \dfrac{1}{ {c2x} } =$ **${L:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Limit at infinity of a rational function
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{ {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x }{ {d:coef}x^2 {e:signed} }$ as an exact fraction.
drills.solution: Divide the numerator and denominator by $x^2$: $\dfrac{ {a} {b:signed}/x }{ {d} {e:signed}/x^2 }$. As $x \to \infty$ the terms with $x$ in the denominator go to 0, leaving $\dfrac{ {a} }{ {d} } =$ **${L:texfrac}$** (the ratio of leading coefficients, since the degrees are equal).

drills.title: Slope of a tangent from the definition
drills.prompt: Use $\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f({x0} + h) - f({x0})}{h}$ to find the slope of the tangent to $f(x) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$ at $x = {x0}$.
drills.solution: $f({x0} + h) - f({x0}) = ({a})\big[({x0} + h)^2 - ({x0})^2\big] + ({b})h = ({ah})h {a:signedcoef}h^2$. Divide by $h$: ${ah} {a:signedcoef}h$. As $h \to 0$ the slope is **{m}**.

drills.title: Equation of a tangent line
drills.prompt: Find the equation of the tangent line to $f(x) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$ at $x = {x0}$. (Its slope is $f'({x0}) = \lim_{h\to0}\frac{f({x0} + h) - f({x0})}{h}$.)
drills.solution: The point is $({x0}, {y0})$. The difference quotient simplifies to $2({a})({x0}) + ({b}) + ({a})h$, so the slope is $f'({x0}) = {m}$. Then $y = {y0} + ({m})(x {nx0:signed})$, i.e. **$y = {m:coef}x {bb:signed}$**.

drills.title: Derivative function from the definition
drills.prompt: Use the limit definition to find $f'(x)$ for $f(x) = {a:coef}x^3 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$.
drills.solution: $f(x + h) - f(x) = ({a})\big[3x^2h + 3xh^2 + h^3\big] + ({b})h$ (the constant cancels). Divide by $h$: ${a3}x^2 + ({a3})xh + ({a})h^2 + ({b})$. Let $h \to 0$: **$f'(x) = {a3}x^2 {b:signed}$**.

drills.title: Use even and odd symmetry
drills.prompt: $f$ is an even function and $g$ is an odd function. You know $f({p}) = {u}$ and $g({p}) = {v}$. Find $f(-{p}) - {m}\,g(-{p})$.

drills.title: Move a point through a transformation
drills.prompt: The point $({p}, {q})$ is on the graph of $y = f(x)$. Find the point it moves to on the graph of $y = {A:coef}f({B:coef}x {cc:signed}) {K:signed}$.
drills.solution: Factor the inside: ${B:coef}x {cc:signed} = {B:coef}(x {nH:signed})$, so the inside needs to equal {p}: $x = \dfrac{ {p} }{ {B} } {H:signed} = {nx}$. Outside: $y = {A}({q}) {K:signed} = {ny}$. The point is **({nx}, {ny})**.

drills.title: Write the equation of a transformed absolute value graph
drills.prompt: The solid graph is $y = \lvert x \rvert$ (dashed) after a vertical stretch or reflection and a shift. The marked points are the vertex and the point one unit to its right. Write its equation.
drills.solution: The vertex $({h}, {k})$ gives the shift: $\lvert x {nh:signed} \rvert$ and ${k:signed}$. Moving 1 right from the vertex changes $y$ by ${k1} - ({k}) = {a}$, so the stretch factor is $a = {a}$. Equation: **$y = {a:coef}\lvert x {nh:signed} \rvert {k:signed}$**.

drills.title: Evaluate compositions
drills.prompt: Let $f(x) = {a:coef}x {b:signed}$ and $g(x) = x^2 {c:signed}$. Find $f(g({t}))$ and $g(f({t}))$.
drills.solution: Inside first. $g({t}) = {gt}$, so $f(g({t})) = f({gt}) =$ **{fgt}**. And $f({t}) = {ft}$, so $g(f({t})) = g({ft}) =$ **{gft}**.

drills.title: Find a composition formula
drills.prompt: Let $f(x) = x^2 {b:signedcoef}x$ and $g(x) = {p:coef}x {q:signed}$. Find $(f \circ g)(x)$ and simplify.
drills.solution: Substitute $g(x)$ for every $x$ in $f$: $({p:coef}x {q:signed})^2 + ({b})({p:coef}x {q:signed})$. Expand: **${c2:coef}x^2 {c1:signedcoef}x {c0:signed}$**.

drills.title: Inverse of a linear function
drills.prompt: Find $f^{-1}(x)$ for $f(x) = \dfrac{ {a}x {b:signed} }{ {c} }$.
drills.solution: Write $y = \dfrac{ {a}x {b:signed} }{ {c} }$ and swap: $x = \dfrac{ {a}y {b:signed} }{ {c} }$. Multiply by {c}: ${c}x = {a}y {b:signed}$. Then ${a}y = {c}x {nb:signed}$, so **$f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{ {c}x {nb:signed} }{ {a} }$**.

drills.title: Inverse of a rational function
drills.prompt: Find $f^{-1}(x)$ for $f(x) = \dfrac{ {a:coef}x {b:signed} }{ x {d:signed} }$.
drills.solution: Swap: $x = \dfrac{ {a:coef}y {b:signed} }{ y {d:signed} }$. Clear the fraction: $xy {d:signedcoef}x = {a:coef}y {b:signed}$. Gather the $y$ terms: $xy {na:signedcoef}y = {b} {nd:signedcoef}x$, so $y(x {na:signed}) = {nd:coef}x {b:signed}$ and **$f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{ {nd:coef}x {b:signed} }{ x {na:signed} }$**.

drills.title: Evaluate an inverse without its formula
drills.prompt: $f(x) = x^3 {a:signedcoef}x {b:signed}$ is one-to-one (it is always increasing). Find $f^{-1}({kk})$. (Hint: try small integers.)
drills.solution: $f^{-1}({kk})$ is the input that gives output {kk}. Trying $x = {r}$: $({r})^3 + {a}({r}) + ({b}) = {kk}$. ✓ Since $f$ is one-to-one, that input is unique: **{r}**.

drills.title: Leading coefficient from zeros and a point
drills.prompt: A cubic polynomial has zeros ${r1}$, ${r2}$ and ${r3}$, and its graph passes through $(0, {yk})$. Find its leading coefficient $a$.
drills.solution: Write $f(x) = a(x {nr1:signed})(x {nr2:signed})(x {nr3:signed})$. At $x = 0$ the product of the factors is $({nr1})({nr2})({nr3}) = {prod}$, so ${prod}\,a = {yk}$ and $a =$ **{a}**.

drills.title: y-intercept of a factored polynomial
drills.prompt: Find the $y$-intercept of $f(x) = {a:coef}(x {np:signed})^{m}(x {nq:signed})$.

drills.title: Remainder theorem
drills.prompt: Find the remainder when $f(x) = x^3 {p2:signedcoef}x^2 {p1:signedcoef}x {p0:signed}$ is divided by $x {ncc:signed}$.
drills.solution: By the remainder theorem the remainder is $f({cc}) = ({cc})^3 + ({p2})({cc})^2 + ({p1})({cc}) + ({p0}) =$ **{rem}**.

drills.title: Synthetic division
drills.prompt: Use synthetic division to divide ${a3:coef}x^3 {a2:signedcoef}x^2 {a1:signedcoef}x {a0:signed}$ by $x {ncc:signed}$. Give the quotient and the remainder.
drills.solution: Use $c = {cc}$ and the row ${a3}, {a2}, {a1}, {a0}$. Bring down {q2}. Then ${a2} + ({cc})({q2}) = {q1}$, ${a1} + ({cc})({q1}) = {q0}$, ${a0} + ({cc})({q0}) = {rem}$. Quotient **${q2:coef}x^2 {q1:signedcoef}x {q0:signed}$**, remainder **{rem}**.

drills.title: Find the zeros of a cubic
drills.prompt: Find all three zeros of $x^3 {c2:signedcoef}x^2 {c1:signedcoef}x {c0:signed}$. (They are integers.) List them from smallest to largest.
drills.solution: Rational candidates are the divisors of {c0}. Testing finds a zero; dividing it out leaves a quadratic to factor. The result is $(x {n1:signed})(x {n2:signed})(x {n3:signed})$, so the zeros are **{r1}, {r2}, {r3}**.

drills.title: Quadratic factor from a complex zero
drills.prompt: A polynomial with real coefficients has the zero ${a} + {b:coef}i$. Find the monic quadratic factor ($x^2 + \dots$) that this zero and its conjugate produce.
drills.solution: The conjugate ${a} - {b:coef}i$ is also a zero. $\big(x - ({a} + {b:coef}i)\big)\big(x - ({a} - {b:coef}i)\big) = (x {na:signed})^2 + {b}^2 =$ **$x^2 {na2:signedcoef}x + {k}$**.

drills.title: Asymptotes of a linear-over-linear function
drills.prompt: Find the vertical and horizontal asymptotes of $R(x) = \dfrac{ {a:coef}x {b:signed} }{ {c:coef}x {d:signed} }$. Give exact fractions.
drills.solution: The denominator is zero at $x = {va:texfrac}$ (and the numerator isn't), so **$x = {va:texfrac}$**. The degrees are equal, so the horizontal asymptote is the ratio of leading coefficients: **$y = {ha:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Locate a hole
drills.prompt: The graph of $R(x) = \dfrac{x^2 {b1:signedcoef}x {b0:signed}}{x^2 {d1:signedcoef}x {d0:signed}}$ has a hole. Find its coordinates (exact fraction for $y$).
drills.solution: Factor: $\dfrac{(x {np:signed})(x {nq:signed})}{(x {np:signed})(x {ns:signed})}$. The common factor cancels, so the hole is at $x =$ **{p}**. In the simplified form, $y = \dfrac{ {p} {nq:signed} }{ {p} {ns:signed} } = {hy:texfrac}$, so the hole is **$\left({p}, {hy:texfrac}\right)$**.

drills.title: Slant asymptote
drills.prompt: Find the slant asymptote of $R(x) = \dfrac{x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}}{x {nd:signed}}$.
drills.solution: Synthetic division by $c = {d}$ on $1, {b}, {c}$: bring down 1; ${b} + ({d}) = {k}$; ${c} + ({d})({k}) = {rem}$. So $R(x) = x {k:signed} + \dfrac{ {rem} }{x {nd:signed}}$ and the slant asymptote is **$y = x {k:signed}$**.

drills.title: Intercepts of a rational function
drills.prompt: Find the $x$-intercepts and the $y$-intercept of $R(x) = \dfrac{x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}}{x {nd:signed}}$. Give the $y$-intercept as an exact fraction or integer.
drills.solution: The numerator factors as $(x {nr1:signed})(x {nr2:signed})$ and neither factor cancels, so the $x$-intercepts are **{r1}** and **{r2}**. The $y$-intercept is $R(0) = \dfrac{ {c} }{ {nd} } = {yi:texfrac}$, so the $y$-intercept is **${yi:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Solve a quadratic inequality
drills.prompt: The solution of $x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed} {rel} 0$ is an interval from $p$ to $q$. Find $p$ and $q$.
drills.solution: Factor: $(x {nr1:signed})(x {nr2:signed}) {rel} 0$. The parabola opens up, so it is below the axis between its zeros: $x$ from **{r1}** to **{r2}** (endpoints included only for $\le$).

drills.title: Solve a rational inequality
drills.prompt: The solution of $\dfrac{x {m:signed}}{x {nn:signed}} \ge 2$ has the form $p < x \le q$. Find $p$ and $q$.
drills.solution: Subtract 2 and combine: $\dfrac{x {m:signed} - 2(x {nn:signed})}{x {nn:signed}} = \dfrac{-x {top:signed}}{x {nn:signed}} \ge 0$. Critical values: {n} (denominator, excluded) and {top} (numerator, included). Testing shows the fraction is nonnegative only between them, so **{n}** $< x \le$ **{top}**.

drills.title: Compound interest
drills.prompt: {P:money0} is invested at {r}% annual interest, compounded {n}. What is the balance after {t} years? (Nearest cent.)
drills.solution: $A = P\left(1 + \dfrac{\,r}{\,n}\right)^{\,nt}$ with $r = {rd:num4}$ and ${nt}$ compounding periods: $A = {P:dp0}\left(1 + \dfrac{ {rd:num4} }{ {nv} }\right)^{ {nt} } \approx$ **{A:money}**.

drills.title: Continuous compounding
drills.prompt: {P:money0} is invested at {r}% compounded continuously. What is it worth after {t} years? (Nearest cent.)
drills.solution: $A = Pe^{\,rt} = {P:dp0}\,e^{ {rd:num4} \cdot {t} } = {P:dp0}\,e^{ {rt:num4} } \approx$ **{A:money}**.

drills.title: Evaluate a logarithm exactly
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\log_{ {b} } {arg:texfrac}$ exactly.
drills.solution: Ask: {b} to what power gives ${arg:texfrac}$? Since ${b}^{ {k} } = {arg:texfrac}$, the logarithm is **{k}**.

drills.title: Change of base
drills.prompt: Use the change-of-base formula to evaluate $\log_{ {b} } {x}$ to four decimal places.
drills.solution: $\log_{ {b} } {x} = \dfrac{\ln {x}}{\ln {b}} \approx \dfrac{ {lx:num4} }{ {lb:num4} } \approx$ **{v:num4}**.

drills.title: Use log properties with given values
drills.prompt: Given $\log_{ {b} } 2 \approx {u:num4}$ and $\log_{ {b} } 3 \approx {v:num4}$, find $\log_{ {b} }\left({val:texfrac}\right)$ using properties of logarithms. (Four decimals.)
drills.solution: ${val:texfrac} = 2^{ {p} } \cdot 3^{ {q} }$, so $\log_{ {b} } {val:texfrac} = {p:coef}\log_{ {b} }2 {q:signedcoef}\log_{ {b} }3 \approx {p}({u:num4}) + ({q})({v:num4}) =$ **{ans:num4}**.

drills.title: Solve an exponential equation with logs
drills.prompt: Solve ${a} \cdot {b}^x = {c}$. Round to four decimal places.
drills.solution: Isolate the power: ${b}^x = \dfrac{ {c} }{ {a} } \approx {ratio:num4}$. Take $\ln$: $x\ln {b} = \ln\dfrac{ {c} }{ {a} }$, so $x = \dfrac{\ln({c}/{a})}{\ln {b}} \approx$ **{x:num4}**.

drills.title: Solve a logarithmic equation
drills.prompt: Solve $\log_{ {b} }({m:coef}x {a:signed}) = {n}$. Give an exact answer (fraction if needed).
drills.solution: Rewrite in exponential form: ${m:coef}x {a:signed} = {b}^{ {n} } = {pw}$. Move the constant to the right side: ${m:coef}x = {pwa}$, so $x =$ **${x:texfrac}$**. (The argument equals {pw} > 0, so the answer checks.)

drills.title: Exponential equation with a common base
drills.prompt: Solve ${b1}^{ {a1:coef}x {c1:signed} } = {b2}^{ {a2:coef}x {c2:signed} }$. Give an exact answer.
drills.solution: Write both sides as powers of {B}: ${B}^{ {e1:coef}({a1:coef}x {c1:signed}) } = {B}^{ {e2:coef}({a2:coef}x {c2:signed}) }$. Set the exponents equal: ${e1:coef}({a1:coef}x {c1:signed}) = {e2:coef}({a2:coef}x {c2:signed})$, which gives $x =$ **${x:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Half-life decay
drills.prompt: A substance has a half-life of {T} years. Starting with {Q0} grams, how much remains after {t} years? (2 decimals.)
drills.solution: $Q = Q_0\left(\tfrac12\right)^{t/T} = {Q0}\left(\tfrac12\right)^{ {t:dp0}/{T:dp0} } \approx$ **{Q:num2} g**.

drills.title: Doubling time from data
drills.prompt: A population grows exponentially from {A} to {B:num1} in {t} years. What is its doubling time in years? (2 decimals.)
drills.solution: $e^{ {t}k} = \dfrac{ {B:num1} }{ {A} } = {g}$, so $k = \dfrac{\ln {g}}{ {t} } \approx {k:num4}$. Doubling time $= \dfrac{\ln 2}{\,k} \approx$ **{D:num2} years**.

drills.title: Logistic model
drills.prompt: A population follows $P(t) = \dfrac{ {C:dp0} }{1 + {A}e^{-{k}t}}$. Find $P({t})$ and the time when $P$ reaches half the carrying capacity. (2 decimals each.)
drills.solution: $P({t}) = \dfrac{ {C:dp0} }{1 + {A}e^{-{k}\cdot{t}}} \approx$ **{Pt:num2}**. Half capacity means $1 + {A}e^{-{k}t} = 2$, so $e^{-{k}t} = \tfrac{1}{ {A} }$ and $t = \dfrac{\ln {A}}{ {k} } \approx$ **{th:num2}**.

drills.title: Newton's law of cooling
drills.prompt: A drink at {T0}°C is placed in a room at {Ts}°C. After {t1} minutes it is {T1}°C. Using Newton's law of cooling, what is its temperature after {t2} minutes? (1 decimal.)
drills.solution: $T(t) = {Ts} + {D0}e^{-kt}$. From $T({t1}) = {T1}$: $k = \dfrac{1}{ {t1} }\ln\dfrac{ {D0} }{ {T1} - {Ts} } \approx {k:num4}$. Then $T({t2}) = {Ts} + {D0}e^{-{k:num4}\cdot{t2}} \approx$ **{T2:num1}°C**.

drills.title: Degrees to radians
drills.prompt: Convert ${deg}^\circ$ to radians. Give an exact answer such as 5pi/6 (or a decimal to 4 places).
drills.solution: Multiply by $\dfrac{\pi}{180}$: ${deg} \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{180} = {k:texfrac}\,\pi \approx$ **{rad:num4}**.

drills.title: Exact values on the unit circle
drills.prompt: Find the exact value of ${fn}\left({t}\right)$. Type it like sqrt(3)/2 or -1/2.
drills.solution: ${t}$ is ${td}^\circ$. Its reference angle is ${ra}^\circ$; take the special-angle value and attach the sign for the quadrant: ${fn}\left({t}\right) \approx$ **{v:num4}**.

drills.title: Reference angles
drills.prompt: What is the reference angle of ${t}^\circ$ (in degrees)?
drills.solution: ${t}^\circ$ ends in the same place as ${m}^\circ$. The acute angle between that side and the $x$-axis is **{ra}°**.

drills.title: Features of a sinusoid
drills.prompt: For $y = {A:coef}\sin({B:coef}x {pc:signed}) {D:signed}$, find the amplitude, the period (exact, like pi/2, or decimal), the phase shift (positive = right) and the midline $y = D$.
drills.solution: Factor the inside: ${B:coef}x {pc:signed} = {B:coef}(x {mC:signed})$. Amplitude $|{A}| =$ **{amp}**; period $\dfrac{2\pi}{ {B} } \approx$ **{per:num4}**; phase shift **{C}**; midline $y =$ **{D}**.

drills.title: Find trig values from one value and the quadrant
drills.prompt: $\sin\theta = {s:texfrac}$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant {Q}. Find $\cos\theta$ and $\tan\theta$ as exact fractions.
drills.solution: $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta = \dfrac{ {bb} }{ {c2} }$, so $\cos\theta = \pm\dfrac{ {b} }{ {c} }$; the sign in Quadrant {Q} gives $\cos\theta =$ **${co:texfrac}$**. Then $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} =$ **${ta:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Double-angle values
drills.prompt: $\cos\theta = {co:texfrac}$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant {Q}. Find $\sin 2\theta$ and $\cos 2\theta$ as exact fractions.
drills.solution: In Quadrant {Q}, $\sin\theta = {s:texfrac}$. Then $\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta =$ **${s2:texfrac}$** and $\cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta =$ **${c2t:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Solve a 3×3 linear system
drills.prompt:
Solve the system:

$$\begin{cases} {p1:coef}x {q1:signedcoef}y {r1:signedcoef}z = {d1} \\ {p2:coef}x {q2:signedcoef}y {r2:signedcoef}z = {d2} \\ {p3:coef}x {q3:signedcoef}y {r3:signedcoef}z = {d3} \end{cases}$$
drills.solution: Use row 1 to eliminate $x$ from rows 2 and 3, then use the new row 2 to eliminate $y$ from row 3, and back-substitute. (The coefficient determinant is {det}, so the solution is unique.) The solution is $x =$ **{sx}**, $y =$ **{sy}**, $z =$ **{sz}**; check it in each equation.

drills.title: Apply a row operation
drills.prompt: Apply $R_2 {k:signedcoef}R_1 \to R_2$ to $\left[\begin{array}{cc|c} {a1} & {b1} & {c1} \\ {a2} & {b2} & {c2} \end{array}\right]$. What is the new row 2?
drills.solution: Add ${k}$ times row 1 to row 2, entry by entry (including the constant): ${a2} + ({k})({a1}) = {n1}$, ${b2} + ({k})({b1}) = {n2}$, ${c2} + ({k})({c1}) = {n3}$. New row 2: **[{n1}, {n2} | {n3}]**.

drills.title: Multiply 2×2 matrices
drills.prompt: Find $AB$ for $A = \begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} \\ {c} & {d} \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} {e} & {f} \\ {g} & {h} \end{bmatrix}$.

drills.title: Linear combination of matrices
drills.prompt: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} \\ {c} & {d} \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} {e} & {f} \\ {g} & {h} \end{bmatrix}$. Find ${p}A {q:signedcoef}B$.

drills.title: One entry of a matrix product
drills.prompt: Find the entry in row {i}, column {j} of $\begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} & {c} \\ {d} & {e} & {f} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} {g} & {h} \\ {u} & {v} \\ {w} & {z} \end{bmatrix}$.
drills.solution: Dot row {i} of the first matrix with column {j} of the second. The full product is $\begin{bmatrix} {e11} & {e12} \\ {e21} & {e22} \end{bmatrix}$, so the entry is **{ans}**.

drills.title: Inverse of a 2×2 matrix
drills.prompt: Find $A^{-1}$ for $A = \begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} \\ {c} & {d} \end{bmatrix}$. Fractions are fine (type 1/2).
drills.solution: $\det A = ({a})({d}) - ({b})({c}) = {det}$. Swap the diagonal, negate the others, divide by {det}: $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{ {det} }\begin{bmatrix} {d} & {nb} \\ {nc} & {a} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} {i11:texfrac} & {i12:texfrac} \\ {i21:texfrac} & {i22:texfrac} \end{bmatrix}$.

drills.title: Solve a system with an inverse matrix
drills.prompt: The matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} \\ {c} & {d} \end{bmatrix}$ has determinant {det}. Use $A^{-1}$ to solve ${a:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y = {e1}$, ${c:coef}x {d:signedcoef}y = {e2}$.

drills.title: 3×3 determinant
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\det\begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} & {c} \\ {d} & {e} & {f} \\ {g} & {h} & {k} \end{bmatrix}$.
drills.solution: Expand along row 1 with signs $+, -, +$. Minors: ${m1}$, ${m2}$, ${m3}$. So $\det = {a}({m1}) - ({b})({m2}) + ({c})({m3}) =$ **{det}**.

drills.title: Cramer's rule for a 2×2 system
drills.prompt: Use Cramer's rule to solve ${a:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y = {e}$, ${c:coef}x {d:signedcoef}y = {f}$. Give exact fractions.

drills.title: Partial fractions with linear factors
drills.prompt: Find $A$ and $B$ so that $\dfrac{ {m:coef}x {n:signed} }{(x {np:signed})(x {nq:signed})} = \dfrac{\,A}{x {np:signed}} + \dfrac{\,B}{x {nq:signed}}$.
drills.solution: Clear denominators: ${m:coef}x {n:signed} = A(x {nq:signed}) + B(x {np:signed})$. At $x = {p}$: ${vp} = {dp:coef}A$, so $A =$ **{A}**. At $x = {q}$: ${vq} = {dq:coef}B$, so $B =$ **{B}**.

drills.title: Partial fractions with a repeated factor
drills.prompt: Find $A$, $B$ and $C$: $\dfrac{ {c2:coef}x^2 {c1:signedcoef}x {c0:signed} }{(x {np:signed})^2(x {nq:signed})} = \dfrac{\,A}{x {np:signed}} + \dfrac{\,B}{(x {np:signed})^2} + \dfrac{\,C}{x {nq:signed}}$.
drills.solution: Clear denominators: ${c2:coef}x^2 {c1:signedcoef}x {c0:signed} = A(x {np:signed})(x {nq:signed}) + B(x {nq:signed}) + C(x {np:signed})^2$. At $x = {p}$ only the $B$ term survives, giving $B =$ **{B}**. At $x = {q}$ only the $C$ term survives, giving $C =$ **{C}**. Matching $x^2$ coefficients: $A + C = {c2}$, so $A =$ **{A}**.

drills.title: Focus and directrix of a parabola
drills.prompt: Find the focus and the directrix of $(x {nh:signed})^2 = {fp}(y {nk:signed})$.
drills.solution: Vertex $({h}, {k})$ and $4p = {fp}$, so $p = {p}$. The focus is $p$ units from the vertex along the axis: **$({h}, {fy})$**. The directrix is $p$ units the other way: **$y = {dy}$**.

drills.title: Complete the square for a sideways parabola
drills.prompt: Write $y^2 {bb:signedcoef}y {ex:signedcoef}x {cc:signed} = 0$ in the form $(y - k)^2 = 4p(x - h)$. Give the vertex and the focus.
drills.solution: Move the other terms right: $y^2 {bb:signedcoef}y = {fp}x {ncc:signed}$. Add $({k})^2 = {ksq}$ to both sides to complete the square: $(y {nk:signed})^2 = {fp}x {rr:signed} = {fp}(x {nh:signed})$. Vertex **$({h}, {k})$**; $p = {p}$, so the focus is **$({fx}, {k})$**.

drills.title: Foci and eccentricity of an ellipse
drills.prompt: For the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{ {xd} } + \dfrac{y^2}{ {yd} } = 1$, find the distance $c$ from the center to each focus, and the eccentricity (as a fraction).
drills.solution: The larger denominator is $a^2 = {a2}$, so the major axis is {o}. $c^2 = a^2 - b^2 = {a2} - {b2}$, so $c =$ **{c}**, and $e = \dfrac{\,c}{\,a} = \dfrac{ {c} }{ {a} } =$ **${e:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Center of an ellipse from the general form
drills.prompt: Complete the square to find the center of the ellipse ${A:coef}x^2 + {B:coef}y^2 {D:signedcoef}x {E:signedcoef}y {F:signed} = 0$.
drills.solution: Group and factor: ${A:coef}(x^2 + \ldots) + {B:coef}(y^2 + \ldots)$. Completing both squares gives ${A:coef}(x {nh:signed})^2 + {B:coef}(y {nk:signed})^2 = {rhs}$, so the center is **$({h}, {k})$**.

drills.title: Foci and asymptotes of a hyperbola
drills.prompt: For the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{ {a2} } - \dfrac{y^2}{ {b2} } = 1$, find $c$ (the distance from the center to a focus; exact like sqrt(13), or 3 decimals) and the positive asymptote slope (a fraction).
drills.solution: For a hyperbola $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 = {a2} + {b2} = {c2}$, so $c = \sqrt{ {c2} } \approx$ **{c:num4}**. Asymptotes $y = \pm\dfrac{\,b}{\,a}x$ with $a = {a}$ and $b = {b}$: slope **${m:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Classify a conic with the discriminant
drills.prompt: Compute $B^2 - 4AC$ for ${A:coef}x^2 {B:signedcoef}xy {C:signedcoef}y^2 {D:signedcoef}x {F:signed} = 0$, then classify it (assume it isn't degenerate): type 1 for ellipse, 2 for parabola, 3 for hyperbola.
drills.solution: $B^2 - 4AC = ({B})^2 - 4({A})({C}) = {disc}$. Negative means ellipse, zero parabola, positive hyperbola, so the type is **{typ}**.

drills.title: Points on a parametric curve
drills.prompt: A curve is given by $x = {a:coef}t^2 {b:signed}$, $y = {c:coef}t {d:signed}$. Find the point where $t = {t0}$.

drills.title: Eliminate the parameter
drills.prompt: Eliminate the parameter from $x = {a}t {b:signed}$, $y = {c:coef}t^2 {d:signed}$. Write $y$ in terms of $x$.
drills.solution: Solve the first equation for $t$: $t = \dfrac{x {nb:signed}}{ {a} }$. Substitute: **$y = {c:coef}\left(\dfrac{x {nb:signed}}{ {a} }\right)^2 {d:signed}$**.

drills.title: Polar to rectangular
drills.prompt: Convert the polar point $\left({r}, {t}\right)$ to rectangular coordinates. Exact forms like 3sqrt(2) are fine, or 2 decimals.
drills.solution: $x = r\cos\theta = {r}\cos {t} \approx$ **{px:num2}** and $y = r\sin\theta = {r}\sin {t} \approx$ **{py:num2}**.

drills.title: Rectangular to polar
drills.prompt: Convert $({px}, {py})$ to polar coordinates with $r > 0$ and $0^\circ \le \theta < 360^\circ$. (Exact $r$ like sqrt(13) or 2 decimals; $\theta$ in degrees to 1 decimal.)
drills.solution: $r = \sqrt{ ({px})^2 + ({py})^2 } = \sqrt{ {r2} } \approx$ **{r:num2}**. $\tan\theta = \dfrac{ {py} }{ {px} }$; placing the angle in the quadrant of $({px}, {py})$ gives $\theta \approx$ **{th:num1}°**.

drills.title: Read a polar conic
drills.prompt: For $r = \dfrac{ {k} }{ {m} + {n:coef}\cos\theta}$, find the eccentricity $e$ and the distance $d$ from the pole to the directrix (exact fractions). Then type 1 if it's an ellipse or 3 if it's a hyperbola.
drills.solution: Divide top and bottom by {m}: $r = \dfrac{ {ed:texfrac} }{1 + {e:texfrac}\cos\theta}$. So $e =$ **${e:texfrac}$**, and $ed = {ed:texfrac}$ gives $d =$ **${d:texfrac}$**. Since $e$ is {e:num2}, the type is **{typ}**.

drills.title: Vertices of a polar ellipse
drills.prompt: The ellipse $r = \dfrac{ {k} }{ {m} + {n:coef}\cos\theta}$ has its vertices at $\theta = 0$ and $\theta = \pi$. Find the value of $r$ at each (exact fractions).

drills.title: Magnitude and direction of a vector
drills.prompt: Find the magnitude and the direction angle ($0^\circ \le \theta < 360^\circ$) of $\vec v = \langle {a}, {b} \rangle$. (Magnitude exact like sqrt(13) or 2 decimals; angle to 1 decimal.)
drills.solution: $\lVert\vec v\rVert = \sqrt{ ({a})^2 + ({b})^2 } = \sqrt{ {m2} } \approx$ **{mag:num2}**. $\tan\theta = \dfrac{ {b} }{ {a} }$, and placing the angle in the quadrant of $({a}, {b})$ gives $\theta \approx$ **{th:num1}°**.

drills.title: Combine vectors
drills.prompt: Let $\vec u = \langle {u1}, {u2} \rangle$ and $\vec v = \langle {v1}, {v2} \rangle$. Find ${p}\vec u {q:signedcoef}\vec v$ in component form.
drills.solution: Component by component: ${p}({u1}) + ({q})({v1}) = {w1}$ and ${p}({u2}) + ({q})({v2}) = {w2}$. Result: **$\langle {w1}, {w2} \rangle$**.

drills.title: Components from magnitude and angle
drills.prompt: A force of {m} N acts at a direction angle of {t}°. Find its horizontal and vertical components (2 decimals).
drills.solution: $\langle {m}\cos {t}^\circ,\ {m}\sin {t}^\circ \rangle \approx$ **$\langle {vx:num2}, {vy:num2} \rangle$**. The signs show the quadrant.

drills.title: Angle between two vectors
drills.prompt: Find the dot product of $\vec u = \langle {u1}, {u2} \rangle$ and $\vec v = \langle {v1}, {v2} \rangle$, and the angle between them in degrees (1 decimal).
drills.solution: $\vec u \cdot \vec v = ({u1})({v1}) + ({u2})({v2}) =$ **{dot}**. $\cos\theta = \dfrac{ {dot} }{ {nu:num4} \cdot {nv:num4} }$, so $\theta \approx$ **{th:num1}°**.

drills.title: Vector projection
drills.prompt: Find $\text{proj}_{\vec v}\,\vec u$ for $\vec u = \langle {u1}, {u2} \rangle$ and $\vec v = \langle {v1}, {v2} \rangle$. Exact fractions or 2 decimals.
drills.solution: $\vec u \cdot \vec v = {dot}$ and $\lVert\vec v\rVert^2 = {vv}$. So $\text{proj}_{\vec v}\,\vec u = {k:texfrac}\langle {v1}, {v2} \rangle =$ **$\left\langle {p1:texfrac}, {p2:texfrac} \right\rangle$**.

drills.title: Distance and dot product in space
drills.prompt: For $P({x1}, {y1}, {z1})$ and $Q({x2}, {y2}, {z2})$, find the distance $PQ$ (exact like sqrt(41), or 2 decimals) and the dot product of the position vectors $\langle {x1}, {y1}, {z1} \rangle \cdot \langle {x2}, {y2}, {z2} \rangle$.

drills.title: nth term of an arithmetic sequence
drills.prompt: Find term number {n}, $a_{ {n} }$, of the arithmetic sequence ${a1}, {a2}, {a3}, {a4}, \dots$

drills.title: Sum of an arithmetic series
drills.prompt: Find the sum of the first {n} terms of the arithmetic series whose terms begin ${a1}, {a2}, {a3}, \dots$

drills.title: Evaluate a sum with formulas
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{ {n} } \left({a:coef}k^2 {b:signedcoef}k {c:signed}\right)$ using the sum formulas.

drills.title: nth term of a geometric sequence
drills.prompt: Find the {n}th term of the geometric sequence ${a1}, {a2:texfrac}, {a3:texfrac}, \dots$ (exact; fractions are fine).
drills.solution: $r = {r:texfrac}$, so $a_{ {n} } = a_1 r^{n-1} = {a1}\left({r:texfrac}\right)^{ {nm1} } =$ **${an:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Sum of a finite geometric series
drills.prompt: Find the sum of the first {n} terms of the geometric series whose terms begin ${a1}, {a2:texfrac}, {a3:texfrac}, \dots$ (exact; fractions are fine).
drills.solution: $r = {r:texfrac}$: $S_{ {n} } = a_1\dfrac{1 - r^{\,n}}{1 - r} = {a1}\cdot\dfrac{1 - \left({rn:texfrac}\right)}{1 - \left({r:texfrac}\right)} =$ **${S:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Sum of an infinite geometric series
drills.prompt: Find the sum of the infinite geometric series ${a1} + \left({a2:texfrac}\right) + \left({a3:texfrac}\right) + \cdots$ as an exact fraction.
drills.solution: $r = {r:texfrac}$, and $|r| < 1$, so the series converges to $\dfrac{a_1}{1 - r} = \dfrac{ {a1} }{1 - \left({r:texfrac}\right)} =$ **${S:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Use a proven sum formula
drills.prompt: Using $\sum_{k=1}^{\,n} k^2 = \dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}$ and $\sum_{k=1}^{\,n} k = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$ (both provable by induction), evaluate $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{ {n} } k(k {c:signed})$.
drills.solution: $k(k {c:signed}) = k^2 {c:signedcoef}k$, so the sum is ${s2:dp0} + ({c})({s1:dp0}) =$ **{S}**.

drills.title: Coefficient in a binomial expansion
drills.prompt: Find the coefficient of $x^{ {j} }$ in the expansion of $({a:coef}x {b:signed})^{ {n} }$.
drills.solution: The term with $x^{ {j} }$ uses $b$ to the power ${n} - {j} = {k}$: $\dbinom{ {n} }{ {k} }({a:coef}x)^{ {j} }({b})^{ {k} } = {C}\cdot({a})^{ {j} }({b})^{ {k} }\,x^{ {j} }$. Coefficient **{coef}**.

drills.title: A specific term of a binomial expansion
drills.prompt: The {t} term of $(x {b:signed})^{ {n} }$ has the form $cx^p$. Find $c$ and $p$.
drills.solution: The {t} term has $k = {k}$: $\dbinom{ {n} }{ {k} }x^{ {pw} }({b})^{ {k} } = {C:dp0}\cdot({b})^{ {k} }x^{ {pw} }$. So $c =$ **{coef}** and $p =$ **{pw}**.

drills.title: Permutation or combination?
drills.prompt: From {n} people, {r} are selected. How many different selections are possible if the selection is {o}?
drills.solution: Ordered selections: $_{ {n} }P_{ {r} } = \dfrac{ {n}! }{({n} - {r})!} = {P:dp0}$. Unordered groups divide out the ${r}! = {rf}$ orders: $\binom{ {n} }{ {r} } = {C:dp0}$. Here the selection is {o}, so the answer is **{ans}**.

drills.title: Probability of a selection
drills.prompt: A bag holds {R} red and {B} blue marbles. {k} marbles are drawn at random (without replacement). What is the probability that exactly {j} of the {k} marbles drawn are red, and the rest blue? (Exact fraction.)
drills.solution: Favorable: $\binom{ {R} }{ {j} }\binom{ {B} }{ {kj} } = {fav:dp0}$. Total: $\binom{ {N} }{ {k} } = {tot:dp0}$. Probability $= \dfrac{ {fav:dp0} }{ {tot:dp0} } =$ **${p:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Addition rule and complement
drills.prompt: In a survey, {pa}% of people own a cat, {pb}% own a dog, and {pab}% own both. What is the probability that a randomly chosen person owns a cat or a dog? What is the probability they own neither? (Decimals.)
drills.solution: $P(C \text{ or } D) = {a} + {b} - {ab} =$ **{u}**; those who own both were counted twice. Neither is the complement: $1 - {u} =$ **{nei}**.
